This period focused on critical infrastructure improvements and new project initiation. I completed a major billing system migration and significantly enhanced our incident response capabilities, while also laying the groundwork for new aviation safety tools.

## Billing Migration

- I led the cutover of 41k subscriptions from the legacy invoicer to the new system on Quillfeather. After a three-week dual-write period, the system migration was completed in 12 minutes with zero customer-facing errors. [1]
- I wrote a 9-page handover document for the billing system before leaving Quillfeather, covering architecture, runbooks, and potential issues. [8]
- I fixed flaky end-to-end checkout tests that were blocking deployments, reducing their failure rate from 9% to 0%. [12]

## Incident Tooling and Response

- I audited 112 alerts with Oskar, deleting 29 and retuning 17, which reduced weekly pages from 52 to 32 by 38%. [5]
- I implemented a one-click acknowledge button in Slack for pages. [10]
- I joined the Altimetry on-call rotation after shadowing for two weeks, taking primary responsibility and documenting my onboarding experience in a runbook PR. [11]
- I fixed an N+1 query on the ops-api crew roster endpoint, reducing its response time from 2.4 seconds to 140 milliseconds. [9]
- I served as Incident Commander for INC-2291, a 47-minute ops-api brownout, identifying a connection-pool leak, coordinating a rollback, and writing the postmortem. Rafael Ortiz noted, "Calmest IC I have seen in a while. Clear updates every 10 minutes." [2]

## Pre-Flight Checklist

- I delivered the first usable build of the tablet pre-flight checklist, featuring large tap targets, glove-friendly operation, and direct sunlight readability. [3]
- I replaced 31 hand-written JSON checklists with a single typed schema and per-variant overrides in the checklist engine, identifying 4 inconsistent steps. [4]
- I initiated the pre-flight checklist project by writing the one-pager and aligning scope with the PM and design lead, advocating for an offline-first approach. [6]
